reporting-org.narrative: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs

description.narrative: ltpgtThe conflict in Myanmar has escalated dramatically, exacerbating protection risks and amplifying the prevalence of landmines and explosive remnants of war (ERW). In 2023, UNICEF documented an alarming surge in civilian casualties from landmines and ERW, with incidents nearly tripling from 390 in 2022 to 1,052. UNICEF’s Child Well-Being Panel Phone Survey (2023) revealed that 11% of respondents were aware of explosive ordnance threats in their vicinity, and nearly half of the IDP returnee households reported affected members within the last year due to these dangers. Given the active conflict and constraints on humanitarian demining, explosive ordnance risk education (EORE) remains a vital life-saving strategy. Moreover, people with disabilities, disproportionately affected by the conflict, face significant challenges. Among people with disabilities registered in UNICEF’s Disability Management Information system (DMIS), over 13% have never received medical treatment, 58% require assistive devices, 43% of children with disabilities have never attended school, and 88% of youth with disabilities are unemployed or economically inactive. People with disabilities often encounter numerous barriers during emergency responses, including physical obstacles, lack of information, financial constraints, safety concerns, and discrimination.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThe current funding proposal seeks support from the MHF to address substantial funding shortfalls and expand services into six under-served townships in Magway and Sagaing. This funding is critical to ensuring the continuity and expansion of essential services and directly aligns with the Allocation Strategy’s objectives to enhance the mainstreaming of disability inclusion and EORE within ongoing MHF projects. Specifically, the project aims to: strengthen EORE delivery and mainstreaming to safeguard affected communities and humanitarian personnel enhance organisational and partner capacity for a more disability-inclusive response and deliver specialised assistance and services tailored to the unique needs of persons with disabilities and landmine/EO survivors. The geographic focus includes five townships in Sagaing (Kanbalu, Kale, Pale, Tamu, Monywa) and one in Magway (Pakkoku), targeting areas with acute needs and high risks associated with landmines and ERW. This strategic approach ensures a targeted, effective, and sustainable impact, reinforcing UNICEF’s and its partners commitment to enhancing safety and inclusivity in conflict-affected regions of Myanmar.ltbrgtlt/pgt
